47643-mary-lamb.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. friends, who have left written memorials of them--that we are brought nearest; the period, that is, of Charles' youth and early manhood. For Mary was the elder by ten years; and there is but little to tell of the last twenty of her eighty-three years of life, when the burthen of age was added to that of her sad malady.

arxiv-1705-05283.title: Visualizing Dimensionality Reduction Artifacts: An Evaluation Volume: 34 Issue: 3
arxiv-1705-05283.creator: Nicolas Heulot 1,2, Jean-Daniel Fekete 1, Michael Aupetit 2 1 Inria, France, 2 CEA, France May 2015
arxiv-1705-05283.description: Abstract Multidimensional scaling allows visualizing high-dimensional data as 2D maps with the premise that insights in 2D reveal valid information in high-dimensions, but the resulting projections always suffer from artifacts such as false neighborhoods and tears. These artifacts can be revealed by interactively coloring the projection according to the original dissimilarities relative to a reference item.

arxiv-2202-04809.title: Existence of global-in-time solutions to a system of fully nonlinear parabolic equations
arxiv-2202-04809.creator: Takahiro Kosugi and Ryuichi Sato
arxiv-2202-04809.description: Abstract We consider the Cauchy problem for a system of fully nonlinear parabolic equations. In this paper, we shall show the existence of global-in-time solutions to the problem. Our condition to ensure the global existence is specific to the fully nonlinear parabolic system.

arxiv-2204-07402.title: BYOL for Audio: Exploring Pre-trained General-purpose Audio Representations PubID: pubid: PREPRINT
arxiv-2204-07402.creator: Daisuke Niizumi, Daiki Takeuchi, Yasunori Ohishi, Noboru Harada, and Kunio Kashino
arxiv-2204-07402.description: Abstract Pre-trained models are essential as feature extractors in modern machine learning systems in various domains. In this study, we hypothesize that representations effective for general audio tasks should provide multiple aspects of robust features of the input sound. For recognizing sounds regardless of perturbations such as varying pitch or timbre, features should be robust to these perturbations.

arxiv-2310-01943.title: Ravestate: Distributed Composition of a Causal-Specificity-Guided Interaction Policy
arxiv-2310-01943.creator: Joseph Dolp, Andreas Karimi, Negin joseph.birkner@tum.de andreas.dolp@tum.de negin.karimi@tum.de Basargin, Nikita Kharchenko, Alona Hostettler, Rafael n.basargin@tum.de alona.kharchenko@tum.de rh@roboy.org
arxiv-2310-01943.description: Abstract In human-robot interaction policy design, a rule-based method is efficient, explainable, expressive and intuitive. In this paper, we present the Signal-Rule-Slot framework, which refines prior work on rule-based symbol system design and introduces a new, Bayesian notion of interaction rule utility called Causal Pathway Self-information .

arxiv-2310-12033.title: CoDrug : Conformal Drug Property Prediction with Density Estimation under Covariate Shift
arxiv-2310-12033.creator: Siddhartha Laghuvarapu, Zhen Lin, Jimeng Sun
arxiv-2310-12033.description: Abstract In drug discovery, it is vital to confirm the predictions of pharmaceutical properties from computational models using costly wet-lab experiments. Hence, obtaining reliable uncertainty estimates is crucial for prioritizing drug molecules for subsequent experimental validation. Conformal Prediction (CP) is a promising tool for creating such prediction sets for molecular properties with a coverage guarantee.

arxiv-2402-01134.title: DeepAAT: Deep Automated Aerial Triangulation for Fast UAV-based Mapping
arxiv-2402-01134.creator: Zequan Chen, Jianping Li, Qusheng Li, Zhen Dong, Bisheng Yang
arxiv-2402-01134.description: Abstract Automated Aerial Triangulation (AAT), aiming to restore image poses and reconstruct sparse points simultaneously, plays a pivotal role in earth observation. AAT has evolved into a fundamental process widely applied in large-scale Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) based mapping. However classic AAT methods still face challenges like low efficiency and limited robustness.

arxiv-2501-17665.title: Planning with Vision-Language Models and a Use Case in Robot-Assisted Teaching
arxiv-2501-17665.creator: Xuzhe Dang, Lada Kudláčková, Stefan Edelkamp
arxiv-2501-17665.description: Abstract Automating the generation of Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) with Large Language Model (LLM) opens new research topic in AI planning, particularly for complex real-world tasks. This paper introduces Image2PDDL, a novel framework that leverages Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to automatically convert images of initial states and descriptions of goal states into PDDL problems.

arxiv-2503-01462.title: S-R2D2: a spherical extension of the R2D2 deep neural network series paradigm for wide-field radio-interferometric imaging
arxiv-2503-01462.creator: A. Tajja, A. Aghabiglou, E. Tolley, J-P. Kneib, J-P. Thiran, Y. Wiaux
arxiv-2503-01462.description: Abstract Recently, the R2D2 paradigm, standing for “Residual-to-Residual DNN series for high-Dynamic-range imaging”, was introduced for image formation in Radio Interferometry (RI) as a learned version of the traditional algorithm CLEAN. The first incarnations of R2D2 are limited to planar imaging on small fields of view, failing to meet the spherical-imaging requirement of modern telescopes observing wide fields.

arxiv-2509-16301.title: TF-DWGNet: A Directed Weighted Graph Neural Network with Tensor Fusion for Multi-Omics Cancer Subtype Classification Conference: arXiv; arXiv; 2025
arxiv-2509-16301.creator: Tiantian Yang, Zhiqian Chen
arxiv-2509-16301.description: Abstract . Integration and analysis of multi-omics data provide valuable insights for cancer subtype classification. However, such data are inherently heterogeneous, high-dimensional, and exhibit complex intra- and inter-modality dependencies. Recent advances in graph neural networks (GNNs) offer powerful tools for modeling such structure.

arxiv-2510-18693.title: Chiral anomalies and Wilson fermions
arxiv-2510-18693.creator: Michael Creutz
arxiv-2510-18693.description: Abstract The Wilson formulation of fermions in lattice gauge theory provides a unified description of the chiral anomalies in the standard model. The discrete Dirac operator diagonalizes into a series of two by two blocks. In each block the possible eigenvalues either form a complex pair or separate into two real eigenvalues that have specific chirality.

arxiv-2603-08462.title: Reasoning as Compression: Unifying Budget Forcing via the Conditional Information Bottleneck
arxiv-2603-08462.creator: Fabio Valerio Massoli, Andrey Kuzmin, Arash Behboodi

britannica-1911-penarth.title: Penarth (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-penarth.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-penarth.description: Article 'Penarth' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 21), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. parliamentary division of Glamorganshire, Wales, 166 m. by rail from London, picturesquely situated on rising ground on the south side of the mouth of the Ely opposite Cardiff, from which it is 4 m. distant by rail and 2 m. The place derives its name from two Welsh words, “pen,” a head, and “garth,” an enclosure.

plos-pone-0012727.description: PLOS ONE research article. pmc-10523553.title: Healthcare-associated infective endocarditis: source of infection and burden of previous healthcare exposure
pmc-10523553.creator: Mika Halavaara, Kaisa Huotari, Veli-Jukka Anttila, Asko Järvinen
pmc-10523553.description: Objective:Prevention of healthcare-associated infective endocarditis (HAIE) is based on characterization of underlying factors. Our object was to describe the source of infection, microbiological etiology, and healthcare-related risk factors for HAIE.Design:Retrospective population-based study.Patients:Adult patients diagnosed with HAIE during 2013–2017 who resided in the study area in Southern Finland with adult population of 0.9 million.Results:Ninety-five HAIE episodes were included.

pmc-10806106.title: Antigen-presenting B cells promote TCF-1+ PD1- stem-like CD8+ T-cell proliferation in glioblastoma
pmc-10806106.creator: David Hou, Hanxiao Wan, Joshua L. Katz, Si Wang, Brandyn A. Castro, Gustavo I. Vazquez-Cervantes, Victor A. Arrieta, Silpol Dhiantravan, Hinda Najem, Aida Rashidi, Tzu-yi Chia, Tarlan Arjmandi, Jimena Collado, Leah Billingham, Aurora Lopez-Rosas, Yu Han, Adam M. Sonabend, Amy B. Heimberger, Peng Zha
pmc-10806106.description: Understanding the spatial relationship and functional interaction of immune cells in glioblastoma (GBM) is critical for developing new therapeutics that overcome the highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Our study showed that B and T cells form clusters within the GBM microenvironment within a 15-μm radius, suggesting that B and T cells could form immune synapses within the GBM.

pmc-11475905.title: Evaluation of Two Levels of Trace Mineral Supplementation to Beef Calves Prior to Weaning
pmc-11475905.creator: Gracia M. P. Hernandez, Aline C. R. Dos Santos, Matheus F. L. Ferreira, David Bohnert, Juliana Ranches
pmc-11475905.description: Simple SummaryThe trace mineral nutrition of ruminants has been widely studied; however, most of the research has focused on the requirements of mature cattle, and the requirements of trace minerals for calves prior to weaning are poorly understood. This study investigated how two levels of trace mineral supplements provided to beef calves before weaning affect their performance and mineral status.

pmc-11600569.title: New technology: clinical efficacy of intracapsular decompression and supported hollow screw treatment for Garden IV femoral neck fractures
pmc-11600569.creator: Zhaofeng Jia, Tinghui Xiao, Yimiao Lin, Wenjun Huang, Peizhi Deng, Jiandong Lin, Shiyuan Lin, Jiwu Cheng, Fengting Cui, Xinjia Hu, Xiaoming Zhang
pmc-11600569.description: BackgroundThe management of Garden IV femoral neck fractures presents a formidable challenge. This study aimed to assess the safety and efficacy of a novel technological approach for treating Garden IV femoral neck fractures, involving intracapsular decompression and the utilization of supported hollow screws.

pmc-12751624.title: Lessons learned from a decade of re-exploratory laparotomies in obstetrics and gynecology at a tertiary care hospital in Mumbai, India, 2014–2024
pmc-12751624.creator: Rashida Ali, Nimish Tutwala, Mena Abdalla
pmc-12751624.description: BackgroundRe-exploratory laparotomy in obstetrics and gynecology is a serious and challenging surgical event associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Understanding its incidence, indications, and outcomes is crucial for improving patient care and surgical safety. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of re-exploratory laparotomies over a 10-year period in a major tertiary care center.

pmc-12977271.title: Proteomic mapping of Rosa damascena nanovesicles reveals plastid mitochondrial metabolic convergence and antimicrobial peptides
pmc-12977271.creator: Subhashini Brahadeeswaran, Ramasamy Tamizhselvi
pmc-12977271.description: Rosa damascena exhibits diverse biological activities, including antimicrobial, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, cardioprotective, neuroprotective, and skin-protective effects, largely attributed through its rich phytochemical composition. In parallel, plant-derived nanovesicles (PD-NVs) have emerged as natural nanocarriers that transport bioactive cargos capable of modulating recipient cell functions across kingdoms.

pmc-13146616.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1590 VISUALISING 30 YEARS OF THE SOUTH LONDON STROKE REGISTER: A PHOTOVOICE STUDY ON THE HIDDEN IMPACTS OF STROKE
pmc-13146616.creator: Sophie Rowland-Coomber, Esther De Gracia Corrales, Herminigilda Elleker, Samm Haillay, Janice Simpson, Eleanor Stevens, Eva S Emmett, Christopher McKevitt, Tayla Schaapveld, Charles Wolfe, Iain Marshall, David Wyatt
pmc-13146616.description: Background and aimsTo mark the impact of 30 years of the South London Stroke Register (SLSR), a photovoice project was undertaken with stroke survivors. The stroke survivors, as co-researchers, decided to focus on the hidden impacts of stroke and how informal support helps individuals with stroke recovery.MethodsFour workshops were conducted, with five stroke survivors.

pmc-13384124.title: Waterpipe use among people who smoke in rural Vietnam: Secondary analysis from the M2Q2 randomized clinical trial
pmc-13384124.creator: Andrew W. Liu, Yvonne P. Nguyen, Narayani Ballambat, Hai Tran, Xuan Nguyen, Julie Flahive, Jeroan J. Allison, Nguyen Vu, Hoa L. Nguyen, Rajani S. Sadasivam
pmc-13384124.description: INTRODUCTIONWaterpipe (WTP) tobacco smoking is highly prevalent in Vietnam. WTP use is associated with higher nicotine exposure and increased risk of pulmonary and cardiovascular diseases. The aim of this study is to understand WTP use and how it may influence smoking behaviors and cessation.

pmc-13556370.title: 564. Genetic liability to suicide attempt and its relationship with depression and stress-related factors
pmc-13556370.creator: D Beliuk, D Torok, G Juhasz, X Gonda
pmc-13556370.description: BackgroundSuicide attempt (SA) is a complex and heritable phenomenon posing a pressing issue in public health and a constant challenge in psychiatry. SA phenotype is strongly associated with psychiatric illnesses, particularly major depressive disorder, yet evidence from genetic and epidemiological studies suggests partially distinct underlying mechanisms.

pmc-13568205.title: Adaptive Residual Correction Network for Efficient Single Image Super-Resolution
pmc-13568205.creator: Jinsha Tian, Junyu Guo, Bingbin Feng, Hongjin Zhu, Yang Luo
pmc-13568205.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In recent years, vision transformers have demonstrated remarkable superiority to CNNs in single image super-resolution (SISR), yet their heavy computational and storage costs hinder practical deployment. In this work, we revisit CNN-based residual learning for SISR and identify a specific yet overlooked problem: the residual signal is often biased by mapping errors during model training, and this bias can propagate and accumulate through layers.
